33.0.0.en: The king seized Jeremiah and cast him into prison because he had prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem. But the tender God spoke to him in the prison to make him feel His presence with him, so that he would be reassured and comforted.

33.0.1.en: God reveals Himself to you in afflictions to reassure you, guide you and gladden your heart. So do not be disturbed by the affliction, for it may be the best time in which you experience God's love and know Him closely.

33.1.0.en: The Lord declares that He is the maker of the earth and its former, in order to reassure the imprisoned Jeremiah. For although Jeremiah was bound in a dark chamber, God declares to him that He is the maker of the whole earth upon which all men live, so he need not be troubled by the chains, because God, the Ruler of all, upholds him and speaks with him. This is the second consolation in the prison, after the first mentioned in (v. 1). The third consolation is that God declares His name to him, which is “Jehovah,” that is, God is, and exists. He thereby assures him of His presence with him so that he does not feel loneliness and isolation inside the prison. For though he has been cut off from men, he enjoys the fellowship of God.

33.2.0.en: Hidden things: the plural of a hard thing, that is, something difficult to perceive and understand.

33.2.1.en: The fourth encouragement is God's invitation to Jeremiah to speak with Him in prayer, so that he is comforted and feels the presence of God. Even greater than this, God promises him to reveal to him wonderful and lofty things of His wisdom that a man, however intelligent, cannot know.

33.2.2.en: Thus we sense the distinction of the spiritual man, in the hardest circumstances, because God blesses him and magnifies him.

33.3.s.en: (2) The blessings of those who return from the captivity

33.3.0.en: The mounts: the plural of a mound, which is a wall built around a besieged city to prevent those in it from escaping. The enemies build them so that everyone in the city perishes, and the enemies take cover behind these mounds. The engines: long tubes from which they hurl stones or flaming fire onto the besieged cities to burn them.

33.3.1.en: God speaks to Jeremiah, while he is in prison, about the destruction of Jerusalem, and specifies the houses and palaces of the great men and kings in it, which will all be destroyed when the Babylonians besiege it, build mounds around it, and hold in their hands the engines with which to demolish Jerusalem and burn it.

33.3.2.en: And when He says “thrown down by the mounts,” He means thrown down because of the mounds.

33.4.0.en: The carcases of men: the stinking corpses of men whom the Babylonians killed.

33.4.1.en: God calls to His people who come to fight the Babylonians who are attacking them, and tells them that the Babylonians will kill many of the Jews and throw their corpses in the streets until they become putrid and their smell foul.

33.4.2.en: God allowed the Babylonians to strike them, for they are the rod of God with which He strikes His people in His anger, and hides His tender face from them because of the multitude of their sins and their disobedience to God. He disciplines them severely so that they repent, and when they repent He forgives them and blesses them.

33.5.0.en: Health: a strip of linen cloth with which a wound is bound, similar to medical gauze today. Cure: various ointments and medicines for treating wounds and diseases.

33.5.1.en: God shows His mercies to His people whom He brings back from the captivity. He heals their wounds by putting medicines on the injured place, binding it and covering it with the bandage. By this comparison He means that He treats their sins and moves them to repentance, and purifies their senses and thoughts so that they regain their peace. God puts in their hearts the love of faithfulness, that is, truth, so that they hold fast to God's commandments and are mindful of their God in all their conduct, and He increases for them feelings of reassurance and inclination to the truth.

33.5.2.en: God is ready to heal all the problems you have caused by your falling into sin, if you repent and return to Him. So do not be disturbed by the bad state you have reached, but rise quickly and offer repentance and contrition before God to begin a new life full of peace, joy and pure conduct.

33.6.0.en: God promises His repentant people that He will bring them back from the captivity, build their cities and strengthen them spiritually and psychologically, because the discipline was because of sin, and if they repent He will restore to them all their glory.

33.7.0.en: After God had treated the problems of sin that had resulted in the souls of His children, the blessings began, as He filled them with peace and security. After that He restored to them their building and their glory, and in this verse He added a fourth blessing, the forgiveness of their sins and their cleansing from all evil, that is, the removal of the inclination to sin from within them, and not only the blotting out of their sins and forgetting them, so that they enjoy a new heart inclined to a pure life with God.

33.8.0.en: The fifth blessing for those returning from the captivity is that they become God's witness among the Gentiles because of God's care for them and His making them happy with His gifts, so they become a light to the world, calling to faith in God. For the Gentiles sense God's power in His people, so they fear Him and glorify Him together with His people, who praise Him and rejoice in Him.

33.9.0.en: The sixth blessing is the turning of the sorrow over Jerusalem and its surroundings, destroyed by the hand of the Babylonians, into joy over its rebuilding and glory, and the multitude of its inhabitants and their possessions of cattle. They express this joy in four ways:

33.9.1.en: 1- They sing songs of victory with joy.

33.9.2.en: 2- They hold marriages and the bridegroom and the bride rejoice. This is a type of the joy of the people, as a virgin, in God, the Bridegroom of their souls.

33.9.3.en: 3- They praise the merciful God, who restored glory to His repentant children.

33.9.4.en: 4- They offer peace offerings in thanksgiving to God on the bronze altar in the temple, which are a type of the sacrifice of Christ, His Body and Blood, on the altar of the New Testament.

33.10.0.en: The seventh blessing is the multitude of their possessions of sheep and cattle. Instead of the total destruction of the cities and pastures, the folds, that is, the dwellings of the shepherds, will increase, and their flocks will multiply, so that the shepherd counts them one by one. This will be in all the cities of the Jews returning from the captivity, of which He mentions examples, namely the cities of the mountains, and likewise the cities of the valley and the cities of the south, and also in the cities of Benjamin, and not only the tribe of Judah. This is a type of Christ the Good Shepherd, whose believers multiply, and He counts them and cares for them one by one.

33.11.0.en: Days: what is meant is the days of the return from the captivity or the birth of Christ.

33.11.1.en: The good thing: God's promises to the fathers.

33.11.2.en: These are prophecies about the return from the captivity, and this is the near meaning of the prophecy, for God in His goodness grants His people that a Branch of righteousness should grow up to them, that is, the life of righteousness begins in them, so that after their return from the captivity they live in purity of heart, in unity and not as two separated kingdoms.

33.11.3.en: As for the far meaning of the prophecy, it speaks of the awaited Messiah, and the days are the fullness of time when Christ is born. He likens Him to a branch that grows from the tree, which is the Jewish nation, but He is a Branch of righteousness, that is, without sin, and righteous and holy, to lead His people who believe in Him in the life of righteousness. He rules with justice and uprightness, for He rejects evil and rewards His children in the Kingdom of Heaven, while the wicked are cast into eternal torment. With the coming of the awaited Messiah, God's promises that He spoke to the fathers are fulfilled.

33.12.0.en: Christ gives to those who believe in Him salvation from sin and its punishment, that is, eternal torment, and gives to Jerusalem, that is, His Church, peace and righteousness. His children trust that their righteousness is from Him and rejoice to be named Christians, after Christ, the cause and source of their righteousness; that is, they call us “The LORD our righteousness.”

33.13.0.en: Thus God's promises are fulfilled that the reign of the offspring of David will continue through Christ, who reigns over the hearts of those who believe in Him forever. What is meant by Israel is not only the people of the Jews of old but the new Israel, that is, those who believe in the awaited Messiah, who are the Christians.

33.14.0.en: God also promises the continuation of the priesthood among His people, not only through their return from the captivity and the renewal of the temple and the offering of the burnt offerings, sacrifices and oblations that they offer and burn on the bronze altar, but also the priesthood and the ministry of the Levites continue in the New Testament in the form of priests and deacons, not after the order of Aaron, but the priests of the Church who offer the sacrifice of Christ, His Body and Blood. The work of the priesthood continues in a spiritual form in the Kingdom of Heaven in the form of the twenty-four elders, and the unceasing praise of the believers forever.

33.14.1.en: God's promises are true and He cannot break them. This should reassure you greatly however much the afflictions around you increase. So trust that He is with you, upholding you, and even turning all your afflictions into blessings, spiritual growth, and peace and joy that cannot be expressed.

33.15.0.en: The wicked Jews raised doubts about God's promises of His care for His people when they saw the Babylonian attack and Jeremiah's prophecies about the destruction of Jerusalem, and they said that God had broken His covenant with His people. So God sent His word by the mouth of Jeremiah, addressing these wicked people and telling them: if you doubt the succession of night and day, then you doubt My promise to My people that the offspring of David will be king over them.

33.15.1.en: And He says “you have broken,” that is, by the words of your doubts you speak against God. Just as the order of night and day is fixed, so My covenant is fixed with My people and with the offspring of David, and also with the priesthood that I placed among them.

33.16.0.en: God confirms His promises to His people, not only by the firmness of the kingdom for the offspring of David and likewise the priesthood, but also by the multitude of the people like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea, and He will also multiply the Levites, the servants of God.

33.17.0.en: God continues His words with Jeremiah about the murmuring people who spread doubts that God had broken His covenant with them and that He would destroy the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah and scatter them among the Gentiles, so that they would no longer be a nation and a people before Him. This will of course not happen, because God will bring them back from the captivity with great power and restore to them their glories after they repent through the disciplines of the captivity.

33.18.0.en: God confirms a second time that if the order of nature, which is the succession of night and day, were to change, then God would break His covenant with His people and destroy them. This will of course not happen. Just as God preserves the order of night and day until the end of the world, so He also makes the offspring of David kings over His people Israel. God will bring His people back from the captivity, and in the fullness of time Christ will come and reign over the hearts of those who believe in Him, His new people.

33.18.1.en: Be faithful in your promises to God, and if you have been careless in them, return again and renew your vows to live with Him and serve Him, whatever your weakness, relying on His power and help.

33.18.2.en: The breaking of the covenant by freeing the slaves

34.0.0.en: Jeremiah specifies the time of the prophecy, which is the final siege of Jerusalem, when Nebuchadnezzar besieged the city with his army, and with him were soldiers from the lands he had conquered. He had triumphed in all his battles, and Jerusalem remained, which he was now besieging to take it, together with all the cities belonging to it in the kingdom of Judah. This was accomplished in the year 587 BC.

34.1.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to go and meet Zedekiah king of Judah and to repeat to him God's decision that Nebuchadnezzar would take Jerusalem and burn it. This was a last attempt by God that Zedekiah and all his people might repent, so that God would have mercy on them and deliver them. But despite the king's respect for Jeremiah, he was not obedient to God's word and did not repent of his sins.

34.2.0.en: This prophecy adds a second matter, after the decision to burn Jerusalem, which is the seizing of King Zedekiah by the soldiers of Nebuchadnezzar. The third matter is Zedekiah's standing before Nebuchadnezzar and seeing him, and the fourth matter is the carrying of Zedekiah to Babylon, which he would not see with his eyes because they put out his eyes when they seized him.

34.3.0.en: As a result of Zedekiah's listening to Jeremiah's words and honoring him, God gives him grace, so that he does not die by the sword but remains in Babylon until he dies a natural death. This is the fifth matter.

34.3.1.en: God does not forget any virtue that you do. If He rewards the wicked with material blessings in this world, then all the more will He reward you for every good work you do with blessings that are not only earthly but rather heavenly.

34.4.0.en: The burnings of your fathers: it was the custom in ancient times, when one of the kings of the Jews died, that they made a burning for him (2 Chr 16:14) and (2 Chr 21:19). They will lament: they say words of mourning.

34.4.1.en: Ah lord: they glorify you and magnify you.

34.4.2.en: The sixth prophecy is the honoring of Zedekiah at his death as follows:

34.4.3.en: 1- A burning is made for him, as is the custom for great kings.

34.4.5.en: 3- They magnify him at his death.

34.5.0.en: Jeremiah told Zedekiah these six prophecies in Jerusalem.

34.6.0.en: Lachish and Azekah: two fortified Jewish cities lying south of Jerusalem.

34.6.1.en: While Nebuchadnezzar was besieging Jerusalem in its final siege, he was also fighting the two cities of Lachish and Azekah, because they alone remained of the cities of Judah, since Nebuchadnezzar had taken the whole kingdom of Judah, and it remained for him to take Jerusalem, Lachish and Azekah.

34.7.0.en: The Jews were negligent in carrying out the Law of freeing Hebrew slaves in the seventh year (Deut 15:12). When Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem and death drew near them, “King Zedekiah” commanded the Jews to free their brothers who were slaves with them, in the hope that God might remove His anger from them and protect them from Nebuchadnezzar.

34.8.0.en: Zedekiah gathered the leaders of the people, and they swore before God to carry out the Law by freeing their brothers who were slaves, and they carried out the king's command and released the slaves. This shows their obedience to the commandment in the hour of affliction and their taking refuge in God.

34.9.0.en: During Nebuchadnezzar's siege of Jerusalem, Hophra, Pharaoh of Egypt, advanced with his armies toward the armies of Babylon that were besieging Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar was afraid and withdrew from Jerusalem to complete his war preparations, that is, he left Jerusalem for a time to return to it. The Jews thought that the crisis had ended, and they saw their fields, in which the soldiers of Babylon had been encamped, empty, so they felt their need of their slaves to cultivate them. During the siege the slaves did not work and cost their masters their food, so they did without them and carried out the commandment because it saved them the expense of feeding the slaves. But after the fields were vacated, it was in their interest to bring back their slaves, so they went back on their oath and their covenants with God and abandoned the commandment, and brought back their Hebrew slaves by force.

34.9.1.en: Submit to God's commandments, even if they are against your material interests, for the commandment is for your good even if you are not convinced of it. And if you have offered repentance, do not go back on it, and if you fall again, repent and return quickly to God.

34.10.s.en: (3) The punishment of those who violate the covenant

34.10.0.en: God reminds them of His freeing them from the bondage of Egypt, and calls it the house of bondmen, and He also reminds them of the covenant that He made with their fathers in the wilderness of Sinai after their exodus from Egypt, when He appeared on the mountain and gave them the commandments and the Law.

34.11.0.en: The covenant between God and His people was in the words of the Law, which commands that if a Hebrew, because of his poverty, is compelled to sell himself, or his family sells him, as a slave to one of his Hebrew brothers, he shall work for his master six years, and his master must release him in the seventh year. But sadly the fathers did not commit to carrying out this covenant and enslaved their brothers by force for more than six years. This law is mentioned in (Ex 21:2; Deut 15:12).

34.12.0.en: God commends His people in the kingdom of Judah in the days of Jeremiah because they renewed the covenant with God in His house, that is, the temple in Jerusalem, declaring their return to carrying out the Law and freeing the Hebrew slaves in the seventh year.

34.13.0.en: God rebukes them because they turned back from their covenant with Him and took back the Hebrew slaves whom they had released because they had completed more than six years, and so they enslaved them again by force and thereby violated the Law of God.

34.14.0.en: God declares His punishment of His people who refused to obey His Law and did not free their Hebrew brothers who worked as slaves for them. So God looses the sword to kill them, and likewise the pestilence to strike them down sick, and the famine to destroy them, and they become an example of a troubled and distressed nation among the nations of the earth because they violated the commandments of their God, so He disciplines them severely. God intends by this that they fear Him and repent of their sins.

34.14.1.en: When you read God's commandments in the Holy Bible that command you to keep away from evil and make you afraid of the divine punishment, return to Him quickly with repentance and shake off every evil pleasure, so that you save your soul and gain your eternity.

34.15.0.en: The way of making a covenant that was prevalent at that time was to slaughter animals such as a calf, cut it into two halves, and have those making the covenant pass between the two pieces of the sacrifice. This is what the leaders of the Jews did: they passed between a calf slaughtered into two halves, declaring their covenant with God to free the Hebrew slaves, but they turned back and violated this covenant. Abraham made a covenant with God in the same way (Gen 15:9-10, 17). The leaders and all the people passed between the two pieces of the calf, and then when they violated their covenant, God punished them by delivering them into the hand of Babylon, which would kill them by the sword, pestilence and famine.

34.16.0.en: The horror of the divine punishment of God's people who violated the covenant appears in Babylon's fierce attack upon them, the killing of many and the throwing of their corpses in the streets, where they are eaten by birds of prey and beasts of the earth, since there is no one to bury these corpses because of their great number and because the rest flee in fear.

34.17.0.en: After Babylon withdrew from its siege of Jerusalem, and God's people thought they had been rid of them and violated their covenant with God and took back their Hebrew brothers as slaves with them, God allows Babylon to return and besiege Jerusalem and destroy it and burn it and seize King Zedekiah and the leaders of the kingdom of Judah, and even kill many of them. It destroys all the cities of the kingdom of Judah, because God commanded their punishment for their disobedience to His Law.
